FINDING_1_stored_vs_exact_floor_tail.meta_reviewers_claim: PIQA's printed p matches the STRICT tail (0.657647) not the DEFINED inclusive one (0.691725)
FINDING_1_stored_vs_exact_floor_tail.MAIN_verification: PARTLY WRONG, and I am recording the correction. PIQA prints p=0.691. My 2e6-draw check: inclusive tail against the exact rational 928/1838 = 0.691218; strict tail = 0.657285. The printed 0.691 therefore matches the INCLUSIVE (correct) convention. The meta-reviewer has the two numbers right and the attribution backwards.
FINDING_1_stored_vs_exact_floor_tail.but_the_MECHANISM_it_names_is_real_and_I: this is the same class as the floor-rounding defect found earlier today on MMLU-Pro. I ran the census across all nine rows: FIVE have stored > exact and therefore carry the hazard -- MMLU-Pro naive, MMLU-Pro item-avg., MMLU, PIQA, BoolQ. On those rows P(max >= stored) excludes the observed outcome and biases p downward, toward 'survives'.
FINDING_1_stored_vs_exact_floor_tail.why_PIQA_matters_pedagogically: PIQA carries the hazard AND has the right p. So the presence of the hazard on a row does NOT by itself mean that row's p was computed wrongly. That is precisely why this needs a guard rather than an assumption in either direction -- and why I did not simply propagate the meta-reviewer's reading.

MAIN_made_it_a_gate.discriminator_control: a table stripped to only the safe rows gives rc=0 -- so the check discriminates rather than flagging everything

If R-claude-stats is right, a different pair of cells falls. Either way something in that paragraph is wrong, but WHICH determines the rewrite.
